title: Defining his style, then leaving Pa Pa Bue for American festivals
summary: He says his playing is free-wheeling Dixieland leaning to swing, like the pop songs played at the first Condon's. The Fessor's Big City Band record sells widely; he leaves Pa Pa Bue after turning down festival offers and returns to do festivals in America around 1975.

bands.name: Pa Pa Bue's Viking Jazz Band

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Wait - to try to resolve this question once and for all -- the way you describe the way you play is simply what -- how?
Well, it's uh, it's just free-wheeling Dixie land style -- it's more swing; it's really more Swing than Dixie - it's Dixie with a swing.
And, it's what was played at the first Condon's in New York--

Yes - we played the pop songs of the day mostly; we didn't play all the old Dixie Land tunes. And, then, the first recording I made in that country was with Fessor's Big City Band and it was a very successful record; they sold thousands and thousands of these things before another company bought them out and now

they're reissued again. And, it's still selling again. So, then, I went with Pa Pa Bue and stayed almost a year with them and, of course, the money was good but not nearly the kind of money I would have made if I had been on my own. And, I had to turn down some wonderful festival offers because I just couldn't pull out of the band and leave them without a trumpet player; there isn't that many great trumpet players there and ones that are there, they're very good and I mean exceptional; they're busy. They're either in the big city or the big radio bands or they're-- they have a responsible day job - some guys work in banks and so n - so, they can't travel. So, that was a problem there. So, I stayed with Pa Pa Bue almost a year and then, of course, at that time, it was about the first opportunity that I got to - some wires and letters for me to come back to America and if I would do the festival. And, uh, that year, I--- that's the first time I came back and I did a whole series of festivals here.
